subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `openclaw notify`/Gateway connected-UI notification contract, or should this fold into the broader Control UI notification architecture?
rationale: The request creates a shell-facing admin broadcast and UI interruption surface with security, targeting, rate-limit, and overlap decisions that source inspection cannot resolve as a pure bug fix.

options.title: Define a core notification contract first
options.body: Specify the Gateway method/event, admin authorization, target semantics, payload limits, UI rendering behavior, and tests before queuing implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader notification work
options.body: Treat #53228 as a concrete use case for #20237 or #93724 so toast/Web Push architecture owns the shared notification model.

options.title: Defer core CLI delivery
options.body: Keep delivery in plugin/Web Push/hook surfaces until maintainers decide a first-class shell command belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Define a core notification contract first
recommendation.body: Specify the Gateway method/event, admin authorization, target semantics, payload limits, UI rendering behavior, and tests before queuing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security boundary decision across CLI, Gateway, and Control UI, and this handle has the strongest current review signal for that boundary.
